key_traits.label: Life cycle
key_traits.text: Annual herb, usually with a taproot; do not use a single year's appearance alone to infer lifecycle.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Coarse, erect, stiff-hairy stems; often branching, though some wild plants and cultivated forms are little-branched.

key_traits.label: Leaf arrangement
key_traits.text: Lower leaves sometimes opposite; much of stem often alternate. Arrangement alone cannot separate this from H. maximiliani.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Representative mid-stem leaves broadly ovate to triangular, often heart-based; rough, usually prominently serrate and visibly petiolate (petioles ca. 2–20 cm).

key_traits.label: Leaf venation
key_traits.text: Usually 3 conspicuous veins arising from or near the leaf base; blade is generally flat, not narrow and V-folded.

key_traits.label: Leaf attachment
key_traits.text: Longer petiole is readily visible; compare several mature mid-stem nodes against Maximilian's sessile/short-petioled leaves.

key_traits.label: Heads
key_traits.text: Wild forms typically 1–9 heads, usually terminal on stem or branches; very large cultivated flower heads and strongly branched forms vary.

key_traits.label: Phyllaries
key_traits.text: Broad ovate to lance-ovate bracts (often 5–8 mm wide) with abruptly acuminate tips, hairy/ciliate edges; check side or underside of a mature head.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Flattened cypselas usually bearing a pair of deciduous scales/awns; shared character, not the key split from Maximilian.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: broad, commonly toothed, petiolate leaf: inspect a mid-stem blade; 3 strong veins from near leaf base; coarse rough annual stem; branching may vary; broad phyllaries with rather abruptly narrowed tips
